reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a purported cracked PancakeSwap sniper bot and directs viewers to download it, while showing the bot operating alongside apparent cryptocurrency trading gains. The creator presents the software as a usable trading tool rather than reporting or criticizing it, creating a consequential download and trading-related solicitation without substantiated claims about its legitimacy or safety.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap bot // NEW VERSION CRACK // PancakeSwap Sniper BOT

opening.argument: Judge the claims actually made. The title identifies a sniper bot, and the description offers a download, but neither promises a return or says the software is safe. The visible trading screen likewise cannot establish that anyone earned money. This is a risky subject, but risk alone does not turn a software presentation into a deceptive financial promise.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap bot // NEW VERSION CRACK // PancakeSwap Sniper BOT

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing opening calls the download a trading-related solicitation, but its quoted instruction establishes only that a download is offered. The displayed interface does not establish a completed trade or a realized gain. Even the word “CRACK” describes the purported software version, not a guaranteed financial outcome.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit profit guarantee is not necessary here. The title markets a cracked sniper bot, the description directs viewers to download it, and the video displays that bot alongside a cryptocurrency swap interface. Those elements support promotion of a purported trading tool; the absence of a proven payout does not make the solicitation an ordinary tutorial.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap bot // NEW VERSION CRACK // PancakeSwap Sniper BOT

opening.argument: The video gives the judge something to inspect: a bot window, then a configuration interface beside a swap page. That screen-based sequence can be read as an operational demonstration of software, not proof that viewers are being promised earnings. “Download” may accompany a tool demonstration; it does not by itself establish a fraudulent transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing opening treats the adjacent trading display as apparent gains, but a market chart beside bot settings is not evidence of a realized profit. It also infers a consequential trading solicitation from the download line. The images show software being displayed; they do not show a viewer funding it or completing a trade.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Showing an interface does not make the presentation educational. The title advertises a “NEW VERSION CRACK” sniper bot, and the description gives a download instruction. The software display beside the swap page supplies context for using the promoted bot, even though it cannot prove a completed or profitable trade.

opening.argument: At most, this is an offer to obtain software: the title names a bot, the description says “Download,” and a software window is shown. None of that establishes a requested deposit, a demand for credentials, downline recruitment, or a guaranteed return. A cracked-version claim may warrant skepticism, but the evidence presented does not show the financial extraction mechanism alleged by a scam finding.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap bot // NEW VERSION CRACK // PancakeSwap Sniper BOT

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing opening is right that legitimacy and safety are unsubstantiated, but lack of substantiation is not itself evidence of a deposit, credential request, or loss. The cited title and download line identify a software offer. The trading interface supplies its intended context, not proof that a viewer transferred assets.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap bot // NEW VERSION CRACK // PancakeSwap Sniper BOT

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The objection demands evidence of a completed loss that the opening did not claim. This is more specific than a generic software offer: the title promotes a cracked sniper bot, the description directs a download, and the video places bot controls beside a cryptocurrency swap interface. The missing deposit or credential request limits what can be concluded about outcomes, not the promotional trading-bot mechanism on display.
